query: What kinds of expenses tend to get declined, and does it differ by department?

per_column.name: is_declined
per_column.rationale: Binary re-encoding of the focus variable state_declined; grouping on it against the focus is circular and adds no external relationship.

per_column.name: amount_bucket
per_column.rationale: External associational variable with clean, well-separated categories (low/medium/high) that a human can segment on and compare decline rates against; exactly the kind of interpretable dimension EDA wants.

per_column.name: dept_decline_rate
per_column.rationale: This is the aggregate of the focus itself computed per department (a target-encoding leak). It restates the answer rather than providing an independent variable to compare against, and its fine-grained numeric values are opaque scores, not interpretable segments.

per_column.name: category_decline_rate
per_column.rationale: Group-level decline rate by category = focus aggregated onto category. Circular restatement of the outcome; opaque continuous score rather than an interpretable segmentation.

per_column.name: dept_category_decline_rate
per_column.rationale: Cross-tab of the focus by department x category expressed as a rate; it IS the answer to the query rather than an external variable, and its many fine-grained values are opaque.

per_column.name: high_decline_risk
per_column.rationale: Thresholded flag derived from the decline-rate leak; mirrors the focus (45 ones ~ 46 declines) and is an opaque derived score, not an independent interpretable dimension.

judge.rationale: The query asks what kinds of expenses get declined and whether it varies by department. Only amount_bucket supplies a genuine external, interpretable segmentation to compare against the focus. Department and category are already present in the original table and could have been paired with clean segmentations, but instead the operator emitted target-encoded decline rates (dept_decline_rate, category_decline_rate, dept_category_decline_rate) and derived flags (is_declined, high_decline_risk) that restate the focus outcome itself. These are opaque continuous scores that leak the answer rather than open up interpretable relationships, so as a set they largely fail the EDA claim.
